supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for kim.nguyen using NTLM, both from 192.0.2.88 and both with a bad-password substatus, at 13:42:35 and 13:43:56 UTC.
At 13:45:23 UTC, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for kim.nguyen using Kerberos from the same source address, 192.0.2.88.

The supplied authentication events do not identify the device or person behind 192.0.2.88, so the failed attempts and subsequent success cannot be attributed to an authorized user or an attacker from these records alone.

On WS-KNGUYEN-01, Explorer wrote a UserAssist registry value whose encoded path corresponds to Microsoft Word during the review window; this does not establish that the network logons originated from that workstation or session.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for the proxy host were not collected from 13:20 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage; this does not by itself establish whether the authentication activity used the proxy.
The supplied authentication records provide a source IP address but no mapped source hostname, endpoint process, or user/session attribution.
claims_not_established: Whether 192.0.2.88 maps to an authorized Copperline device, an external source, or a sanitized address.
Whether the successful Kerberos logon was performed by kim.nguyen or an unauthorized party.
Whether the failed NTLM attempts and successful Kerberos logon were part of one activity or were related to the local activity recorded on WS-KNGUYEN-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Map 192.0.2.88 to a device and network assignment at the event times using DHCP, NAC, switch, firewall, or equivalent records.
Collect source-endpoint authentication and process telemetry for 13:35–13:50 UTC, if the source device can be identified.
Review domain-controller and network records that could attribute the successful logon to a host or session, and confirm with kim.nguyen whether the activity was expected.
